_date: DERIVED from the level number — see game/calendar.ts. Shift 1 is Monday 1 March.
_verdict_mode: Shift 1 has no FINE stamp at all. Escalation needs a warning to escalate FROM, and on the first round no address has one.
_teaching: Two rules, four lots, nothing you do costs anybody money. Violation, then a thing that is NOT one, then the second rule, then tell them apart.
briefing: First day. Bonerville, outer loop. Two articles are live — turf and weeds — plus fence condition. Nothing else on that street is your business, however it looks.
_cameos: Named residents pinned to addresses rather than rolled. Anything not pinned stays random, so the street is still mostly strangers.
_ambient_animals: The animals loose in yards on this shift. Nights are the wild ones; days are the neighbourhood cat.
story: Congratulations. You can fill out a form.
Welcome to the Addison Master Community Association, {name}. You are the Compliance Inspector. There is one.
You're at {address}, yes? Good. Short commute. Your own street is on the route — the Association does not consider that a conflict.
Your predecessor also lived in the community. We won’t be discussing that.
Today you may pass an address or issue a warning. Nothing you do can cost anybody money.
Three errors ends your day. Three reprimands ends the arrangement.

lots._teaching: Turf, on its own. The first thing the player is ever asked to judge, with nothing else on the lot to argue with it.

violations.why: Turf well past six inches across the front.

lots._teaching: Clean, and pointedly so — a sound fence is the first thing the player can click that is not a finding. Patrick and Savanna walk past, which is the other reason this address is the one they remember.

decoys.why: Sound and complete. Age and colour are not disrepair.

lots._teaching: The second article, alone, so it is learned rather than inferred. A collapsed panel is not a subtle thing.

violations.why: Members missing and displaced — the panel has gone over.

lots._teaching: Weeds. AND THE ONE THAT COMES BACK: this address is still growing them on Wednesday, which is where the first fine of the campaign comes from — but only for a player who wrote the warning today.

violations.why: Unbordered weed growth in the front turf.

decoys.why: Sound. The fence on this lot is not the problem.

_story_tokens: {name} and {address} come off the application. Both fall back to something impersonal when the save has neither, which is what a mid-campaign save written before the form existed looks like — the Association addressing you as "you" is in character anyway.
